Open on a single race-result tile against black. It receives a date and classification with a sharp mechanical click.

Another race. Another result. Then another.

The tiles accumulate into a wall. Each tile represents one actual race start, in chronological order. A restrained counter tracks starts. A second counter tracks wins and remains at zero.

Accelerate the accumulation, but pause on a few source-verified near misses and retirements. Give podiums their own visual treatment: they were achievements, not interchangeable failures.

Use ivory typography, dark graphite tiles, and a single vivid pink reserved for the eventual victory. No cars, driver portraits, or broadcast footage.

As the first-win tile approaches, slow down dramatically. Leave a brief silence. Stamp P1.

Pull back to reveal the entire accumulation of starts and that one changed result. End with the driver, race, date, and verified start count. Let the data provide the emotion.
